question: 13 marks the file writes as a note or rest that Sean did not read in those bars. For each number: what is the ink in the orange box?
verbatim: tile 1 is a whole note rest, tile 2 is a stem on a half note, tile 3 is a mark where a stem of an eighth note touches the beam. It's a little bit thicker right there based on the ink, but it's just where a stem meets a beam. Tile 4 is where a stem of an eighth note meets a beam. Tile 5 is the stem of a half note. Tile 6, it is a pretty large box though, similar to tile 2. I don't know if it is actually just the stem or if it's including more. Tile 6 is a sharp. Tile 7 is a small portion of an arc. Tile 8 is a part of a bar line. Tile 9 is a stem and a flag of an eighth note. Tile 10 is half of a flat sign. It cuts off the top of its stem. Tile 11 is half of a quarter rest, the bottom half. 12 again is most of a stem and part of a flag on an eighth note. And 13 is the flag on an eighth note.

answers.2: the stem of a half note
answers.3: where the stem of an eighth note meets the beam (a little thicker there from the ink)
answers.4: where the stem of an eighth note meets a beam
answers.5: the stem of a half note
answers.7: a small portion of an arc
answers.9: the stem and flag of an eighth note
answers.10: half of a flat sign (the box cuts off the top of its stem)
answers.11: the bottom half of a quarter rest
answers.12: most of a stem and part of a flag on an eighth note
answers.13: the flag on an eighth note

ours: His remark 'a pretty large box, similar to tile 2 -- I don't know if it is just the stem or including more' reads as about tile 5 (said between tiles 5 and 6); recorded with tile 5.

compared_with_the_trace.agree: 12 of 13 (tiles 3 and 4: the trace said 'the beam'; Sean says where a stem meets the beam)

differ.6: the trace's look said a dynamic letter p; Sean: a sharp. The file writes a plain F5 quarter there (Litolff glyph/6/0/6/12/5); the page head reader filed a READ head claim on that ink.
